claim: A three-axis code UE ensemble (Top-K token entropy, pseudo-code consistency, self-generated-test behavioral consistency) raises average AUROC from 0.696 (strongest NL-derived baseline) to 0.776 across five code LLMs.
stance_target: L1 occupancy: code UE scored against hidden-test labels
scope_conditions: Python; APPS-Intro/Interview, HumanEval, MBPP; 5 open models 14B-32B
quoted_support: Across five code LLMs, our three-axis ensemble improves average AUROC from 0.696 for the strongest NL-derived baseline to 0.776 (+8.1 points).

breadth.confidence_families: token entropy (Top-K, Sec 2.2), pseudo-code consistency (Sec 2.3), behavioral consistency on self-generated tests (Sec 2.4), baselines Mean Entropy, CodeBLEU consistency, Symbolic Clustering (Sec 3); verbalized only mentioned in Sec 5 advice, not in Table 1
breadth.model_families_and_sizes: Qwen3-14B, Qwen3-32B, Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct, Devstral-Small-2505, DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct (Sec 3 Models)
breadth.base_vs_instruct: not present (searched: base/instruct, pair; only instruct/general+coder models listed in Sec 3)
breadth.post_training_stages: not present (searched: SFT, RLHF, stage comparison)
breadth.reasoning_models: Qwen3-14B/32B are hybrid thinking models but reasoning-enabled status not stated (searched: thinking, reasoning in Sec 3)
breadth.elicitation_formats: pseudo-code plan prompts (Appendix A); no verbal-confidence prompt format evaluated
breadth.benchmarks: APPS-Intro (N=1000), APPS-Interview (N=1000), HumanEval (164), MBPP (500); HumanEval-X for C++/Java/Go/JS (Table 5)
breadth.label_source: pass@1 on official hidden test suite (Sec 2.1, Sec 3 Metrics)
breadth.label_independence: yes: self-generated tests separate from official-test labels (Sec 3 Metrics)

breadth.calibration_metrics: AUROC, PRAUC only; ECE and Brier explicitly not reported (Sec 3 Metrics)

claim: Correctness label is pass@1 on the official hidden test suite; self-generated tests are kept strictly separate and used only as a signal.
stance_target: L1: execution-graded labels with label/signal independence
quoted_support: y is correct iff it passes every test case in the problem's official test suite (pass@1), which is held out and never shown to the model. The self-generated tests used by the functional signal in 2.4 are strictly separate.

claim: The paper explicitly does not report ECE or Brier and leaves downstream utility (selective generation, human review, agentic deferral) to future work, leaving L3-style utility and calibration-metric analysis open for this evaluation.
stance_target: L3 CLEAN-ish component: routing utility; L1 calibration metrics
quoted_support: We do not report Brier Score or ECE: post-hoc rank-normalized scores have no meaningful absolute calibration, and AUROC/PRAUC suffice to assess the underlying signal.

claim: Comment-token entropy is anti-correlated with correctness (AUROC 0.375) and the authors advise against relying on verbalized confidence as a proxy for code correctness, without evaluating verbalized confidence in a reported table.
quoted_support: Practitioners should retain comment tokens when computing entropy-based uncertainty but avoid relying on verbalized confidence as a proxy for code correctness.
